children.label: a
children.prompt: The ball is struck at an angle of $\theta=40^\circ$ to the horizontal. Find the distance $x$ from the ball’s starting position to the location of the third bounce. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.short:
$x\approx3.23$ table-length units.

Equal reflection angles give $x=8-\dfrac{4}{\tan40^\circ}$.
answer.worked:
Let $t$ be the horizontal distance from the starting corner to the first bounce. Equal reflection angles give the same acute angle to the horizontal on each segment.
$$\begin{align*}\tan40^\circ&=\frac{2}{t}\\t&=\frac{2}{\tan40^\circ}.\end{align*}$$
The horizontal distance from the first bounce to the right edge is $4-t$. Returning from the top edge to the bottom edge requires total horizontal travel $t$, so
$$\begin{align*}4-x&=t-(4-t)\\x&=8-2t\\x&=8-\frac{4}{\tan40^\circ}\\x&\approx3.23.\end{align*}$$
The distance is $3.23$ in the same units as the table dimensions.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The ball is struck so that $x=2$. Find the strike angle $\theta$, to 2 decimal places.

answer.short:
$\theta\approx33.69^\circ$.

Use equal reflection angles to obtain $\tan\theta=\dfrac{4}{8-x}$.
answer.worked:
Let $t$ be the horizontal distance to the first bounce. As in part (a), equal reflection angles give $x=8-2t$.
$$\begin{align*}2&=8-2t\\t&=3\\\tan\theta&=\frac{2}{3}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\\\theta&\approx33.69^\circ.\end{align*}$$
